item.title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer AI Model People Can Run on Their Laptop
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. introduced a new AI model that’s light enough to run on a single computer, allowing users to download and customize the technology.

item.title: Record-Low Danube Strains Vital Route for Black Sea Grain
item.description: Black Sea grain exports are facing fresh constraints as record-low Danube levels restrict flows through Romania just as escalating Russian strikes divert Ukrainian grain from Odesa and other ports.

item.title: Hungary Posts Record July Budget Surplus in Magyar Fiscal Pivot
item.description: Hungary posted its largest monthly budget surplus on record in July, extending an improvement in public finances as Prime Minister Peter Magyar seeks to rein in one of the European Union’s biggest fiscal shortfalls.

item.title: JPMorgan Strategists Raise S&P 500 Target as AI Capex Pays Off
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. strategists raised their S&P 500 Index forecast for a second time in two months, citing strong corporate earnings and the payoff from massive artificial intelligence spending.

item.title: NYT CEO Meredith Kopit Levien on Running a Media Brand in the Age of AI
item.description: The Times is no longer just a newspaper.

item.description: In the last decade, the New York Times has remade itself many times over. item.title: Rakuten Earns First Profit in Six Years Due to E-Commerce Jump
item.description: Rakuten Group Inc. earned its first net income in six years thanks to surging growth in its e-commerce and fintech segments, with help from the company’s chatbot.

item.title: Meiji Yasuda Closely Watching Policy Cancellations as Rates Rise
item.description: Meiji Yasuda Life Insurance Co. is examining an industrywide increase in policy cancellations as rising interest rates prompt customers to shift into other financial products, said its Deputy President Atsushi Nakamura.

item.title: South Korea Growth Seen Accelerating to 3.3% on Chip Boom
item.description: South Korea’s economic growth for this year is expected to accelerate further on strong global appetite for semiconductors, according to a Bloomberg survey of analysts, ahead of a Bank of Korea interest rate decision later this month.

item.title: Egypt Headline Inflation Quickens for the First Time Since March
item.description: Egypt’s inflation rate accelerated for the first time since March, disrupting an easing streak that had lasted for much of the ongoing US-Iran war.

item.title: Destry Named Sole Bank Indonesia Chief Nominee to Calm Markets
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto nominated Acting Governor Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate to head the central bank, advancing a hiring process that has attracted attention from global investors since veteran Perry Warjiyo unexpectedly resigned from the post in late July.

item.title: Philippine Central Bank Keeps Rate Hike on Table Despite Weak GDP Growth
item.description: The Philippine central bank is ready to tighten monetary policy further to guide inflation back to target, Governor Eli Remolona said, while adding that there’s less pressure to do so after last quarter’s surprise economic slowdown.

item.title: Adnoc Gas Exploring New LNG Export Plant to Avoid Hormuz Strait
item.description: Adnoc Gas Plc is considering a new gas export facility outside the contested Strait of Hormuz, Abu Dhabi’s latest move to build infrastructure to avoid the critical waterway that has been largely shut during the Iran war.

item.title: TSMC Sales Rise 45% After AI Spending Roars On Despite Jitters
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported a 45% rise in its monthly sales, a sign of sustained demand for AI hardware in the face of market volatility.

item.title: China Humanoid Makers Hold 97% of Global Shipments, Report Says
item.description: China’s humanoid robot makers commanded more than 97% of global shipments in the first half of 2026, according to new industry data affirming the country’s early lead against US rivals in the burgeoning field.

item.title: Why Strong UK Growth Figures This Week Will Bring Little Cheer
item.description: Figures this week are expected to show that Britain enjoyed another quarter of healthy economic growth. The drivers: World Cup football, multiple heat waves and possibly a spurt of front-loaded activity that has become a familiar feature in recent years.

item.title: Copper Holds $14,000 as Weaker US Rate Outlook Boosts Metals
item.description: Copper traded in a narrow range after six straight weeks of gains, fueled by tightening supplies and easing concerns about US interest-rate hikes.

item.title: SNB Rate Forecasts Now Anctipate Hike in Mid-2027 at Earliest
item.description: Swiss National Bank forecasters pushed back predictions for an interest-rate increase, with no move anticipated before next June at the earliest.

item.title: Emerging-Market Stocks, Currencies Gain After Soft US Jobs Data
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies climbed at the start of a new week as expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes eased following Friday’s unexpectedly weak US employment report.

item.title: Euro Zone Set for Firmer Growth After Bumper Second Quarter
item.description: Economic growth in the euro zone is set to quicken after showing surprising resilience to the Iran war, according to a Bloomberg survey of analysts.

item.title: Romania Set to Keep Rates at 6.5%, EU’s Highest, on Political Turmoil
item.description: Romania is likely to hold borrowing costs unchanged at the highest level in the European Union as a lengthy political crisis clouds the economic and inflation outlook.

item.title: Indonesian Stocks Near Bull Market as Economic Worries Recede
item.description: Indonesian stocks advanced, putting the benchmark index once again near bull-market territory, as investor sentiment was buoyed by signs of a resilient economy and easing concerns over potential market downgrades.

item.title: Rotation From Leveraged ETFs Fuel 30% Jump in Korea Small Caps
item.description: South Korea’s small-cap stocks are regaining investor interest after lagging larger peers for much of the year, as restrictions on leveraged exchanged-traded funds tracking heavyweight chipmakers shift money toward Kosdaq names.

item.title: Yen Underperforms G-10 Peers as Intervention Boost Fades
item.description: The yen has underperformed all its Group-of-10 peers this month as the boost from recent intervention fades, putting traders on alert for further official action.

item.title: Wheat Hits Highest in a Week on Supply Disruptions in Black Sea
item.description: US wheat futures jumped to the highest in more than a week, as disruptions to shipping in the Black Sea raised the prospect of supply shortages from the crucial grain-growing region.

item.title: Sony, TSMC to Invest $6.4 Billion in Japanese Sensor Plant
item.description: Sony Group Corp. and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. are in talks to spend a combined ¥1 trillion ($6.4 billion) on their planned image sensor factory in Japan, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: India’s FX Reserves Climb Toward Record on Foreign Inflows
item.description: Stockpile rises for five straight weeks, the longest run since April 2025.

item.title: Shein Valued at $22 Billion to $25 Billion Ahead of IPO, BI Says
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd.’s fast-fashion niche supports a valuation of $22 billion to $25 billion, Bloomberg Intelligence said, putting a fresh marker on one of the biggest questions surrounding the retailer as it prepares for one of the year’s biggest initial public offerings.

item.title: Australia Widens Orders on Chinese Investors in Rare Earths Firm
item.description: Australia has stepped in again to try to force some Chinese investors out of a rare earths mining firm, telling two parties that they will also need government approval before selling their holdings to ensure the shares aren’t sold to any related parties.
